topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: These remarks introduce the final lecture of the course and state its core learning objectives regarding cancer therapies.

topics.label: Conventional Cancer Therapies and Cytotoxic Chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss traditional physical and cytotoxic modalities used to treat tumors along with their associated toxicities and resistance mechanisms.

topics.label: Exploiting Intrinsic Cancer Cell Vulnerabilities and Repair Defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on therapeutic strategies that exploit intrinsic biological vulnerabilities of cancer cells such as hormone dependence, checkpoint loss, and defective DNA repair pathways.

topics.label: Targeted Kinase Inhibitors and Mechanisms of Drug Resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore targeted small-molecule inhibitors directed against hyperactive oncogenic kinases and the subsequent emergence of resistance and drug dependence.

topics.label: Monoclonal Antibodies and Antibody-Drug Conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the use of engineered antibodies to target tumor surface markers directly or to deliver cytotoxic agents into malignant cells.

topics.label: Tumor Immunology and Cell-Mediated Immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how the immune system interacts with tumors and detail therapeutic methods designed to harness or engineer T cells to eliminate cancer cells.

topics.label: Systemic Challenges, Progress, and Future Horizons in Cancer Therapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the overall clinical landscape of oncology, assessing historical progress, current therapeutic hurdles, and prospective directions for patient management.
